back: For real-coefficient polynomials, if $z$ is a root so is $z^*$.

front: (HL) De Moivre's theorem in Euler form?
back: $(re^{i\theta})^n = r^ne^{in\theta}$. Proved by induction for $n \in \mathbb Z^+$; it holds for all integers $n$.

front: (HL) How do you express $\cos3\theta$ in powers of $\cos\theta$?
back: Expand $(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^3$ binomially and equate real parts with $\cos3\theta$: $\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta\sin^2\theta = 4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta$.

front: (HL) If $z = \text{cis}\,\theta$, what are $z^n + z^{-n}$ and $z^n - z^{-n}$?

back: Write $w = r\,\text{cis}(\theta + 2k\pi)$; take $z = r^{1/n}\,\text{cis}\dfrac{\theta + 2k\pi}n$ for $k = 0, 1, \ldots, n - 1$; adjust arguments into $(-\pi, \pi]$.

front: (HL) The $n$th roots of unity and their sum?
back: $z = \text{cis}\dfrac{2k\pi}n$, $k = 0, \ldots, n - 1$, i.e. $1, \omega, \omega^2, \ldots$ with $\omega = e^{2\pi i/n}$. For $n \ge 2$ they sum to 0 (e.g. $1 + \omega + \omega^2 = 0$).

front: (HL) Where do the $n$th roots of $w$ lie on an Argand diagram?
back: On a circle of radius $|w|^{1/n}$ about $O$, equally spaced by $\dfrac{2\pi}n$ — the vertices of a regular $n$-gon.
It is one of four roots: $2, 2i, -2, -2i$. An equation $z^n = w$ ($w \ne 0$) has exactly $n$ distinct roots.

front: (HL) A real cubic has root $2 + i$. Which quadratic factor follows?
back: $2 - i$ is also a root, so $(z - 2 - i)(z - 2 + i) = (z - 2)^2 + 1 = z^2 - 4z + 5$ is a factor.

front: (HL) When does the conjugate root theorem fail?
back: When the polynomial has non-real coefficients. E.g. $z - i = 0$ has root $i$ but not $-i$.
